es.summary: La aspirina es un antiinflamatorio no esteroideo que inhibe irreversible la ciclooxigenasa, reduciendo la agregación plaquetaria y aliviando dolor y fiebre.
key_points: Inhibe irreversible la COX‑1 y COX‑2, disminuyendo tromboxano A2.
Uso profiláctico en infarto agudo de miocardio y angina inestable.
Efectos adversos gastrointestinales y riesgo de sangrado grave.
Contraindicada en alergia a AINE, úlcera péptica activa y trastornos hemorrágicos.

mechanism: Disminuye la síntesis de prostaglandinas y tromboxano A2.
Reduce la agregación plaquetaria por 7‑10 días.
indications: Dolor leve a moderado y fiebre.
Prevención secundaria de infarto agudo de miocardio.
Angina inestable y síndrome coronario agudo.
Profilaxis de eventos trombóticos en pacientes de alto riesgo.
contraindications: Alergia conocida a aspirina o a otros AINE.
Úlcera péptica activa o sangrado gastrointestinal reciente.
Asma sensible a AINE, embarazo en tercer trimestre.
interactions: Aumenta el efecto de anticoagulantes (warfarina, heparina).
Potencia el riesgo de sangrado con SSRIs y corticoides.
Reduce la eficacia de antihipertensivos ACE‑inhibidores.
nursing_care: Evaluar historial de úlcera, sangrado y uso de anticoagulantes.
Obtener pruebas de coagulación (TP, INR) antes de iniciar terapia.
Monitorear signos de sangrado: hematuria, melena, hematomas.
Retener la dosis si el paciente presenta sangrado activo o plaquetas <100 000 /µL.
Notificar al médico ante hemoglobina descendente >2 g/dL o sangrado grave.
patient_teaching: Tomar la aspirina con alimentos o antiácido para minimizar irritación gástrica.
Evitar alcohol y otros AINE mientras esté en tratamiento.
Reportar cualquier sangrado inusual, hematomas o dolor abdominal intenso.
No exceder la dosis recomendada; uso en niños solo bajo prescripción.

outcomes: Sin evidencia de sangrado: ausencia de hemorragia visible en 24 h.
Valores de hemoglobina estables: no disminución >2 g/dL en 48 h.

interventions.action: Evaluar historial de sangrado y úlcera antes de administrar.
interventions.rationale: Identifica factores de riesgo que pueden precipitar hemorragia.

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar resultados de coagulación (INR, TP) antes de iniciar.
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar alteraciones que aumentan el riesgo de sangrado.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de sangrado cada 4 h (hematuria, melena, hematomas).
interventions.rationale: Detección temprana de hemorragia para intervención oportuna.

interventions.action: Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si aparecen signos de sangrado activo.
interventions.rationale: Previene empeoramiento del sangrado y permite ajuste terapéutico.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de reportar cualquier sangrado o dolor abdominal.
interventions.rationale: Fomenta la participación del paciente en la prevención de complicaciones.

en.summary: Aspirin is a nonsteroidal anti‑inflammatory drug that irreversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase, reducing platelet aggregation and relieving pain and fever.
key_points: Irreversibly inhibits COX‑1 and COX‑2, decreasing thromboxane A2.
Prophylactic use in acute myocardial infarction and unstable angina.
Gastrointestinal adverse effects and risk of serious bleeding.
Contraindicated in allergy to NSAIDs, active peptic ulcer, and hemorrhagic disorders.

mechanism: Reduces synthesis of prostaglandins and thromboxane A2.
indications: Mild to moderate pain and fever.
Secondary prevention of acute myocardial infarction.
Unstable angina and acute coronary syndrome.
Prophylaxis of thrombotic events in high‑risk patients.
contraindications: Known allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs.
Active peptic ulcer or recent gastrointestinal bleeding.
Aspirin‑sensitive asthma, pregnancy in the third trimester.
interactions: Potentiates bleeding risk with SSRIs and corticosteroids.
nursing_care: Assess history of ulcer, bleeding, and anticoagulant use.
Obtain coagulation labs (PT, INR) before starting therapy.
Monitor for signs of bleeding: hematuria, melena, bruising.
Withhold dose if patient has active bleeding or platelets <100,000/µL.
Notify physician if hemoglobin drops >2 g/dL or if serious bleeding occurs.
patient_teaching: Take aspirin with food or antacid to minimize gastric irritation.
Avoid alcohol and other NSAIDs while on treatment.
Report any unusual bleeding, bruising, or severe abdominal pain.
Do not exceed recommended dose; use in children only under prescription.

outcomes: No evidence of bleeding: absence of visible hemorrhage within 24 h.
Stable hemoglobin values: no drop >2 g/dL within 48 h.

interventions.action: Assess bleeding and ulcer history before administration.
interventions.rationale: Identifies risk factors that may precipitate hemorrhage.

interventions.action: Obtain and record coagulation results (INR, PT) before initiation.
interventions.rationale: Detects alterations that increase bleeding risk.

interventions.action: Monitor bleeding signs every 4 h (hematuria, melena, bruising).
interventions.rationale: Early detection of hemorrhage for timely intervention.

interventions.action: Withhold dose and notify physician if active bleeding signs appear.
interventions.rationale: Prevents worsening of bleeding and allows therapeutic adjustment.

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of reporting any bleeding or abdominal pain.
interventions.rationale: Encourages patient participation in complication prevention.

key_points.1.quote: Drug Dosage For acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina: 325 mg orally (chewed) once.

key_points.2.quote: The risk of serious bleeding in the stomach, gastrointestinal tract, brain, and spinal cord is increased with aspirin and other NSAIDs .

sections.indications.0.quote: Indications Mild pain Platelet inhibition in suspected AMI or unstable angina

sections.indications.2.quote: Indications Mild pain Platelet inhibition in suspected AMI or unstable angina

sections.contraindications.0.quote: Contraindications to aspirin are allergy to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), asthma, hemophilia, and other blood clotting disorders.

sections.contraindications.2.quote: Contraindications to aspirin are allergy to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), asthma, hemophilia, and other blood clotting disorders.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Aspirin can cause gastritis and bleeding in the stomach, other parts of the gastrointestinal tract, brain, and spinal cord.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Aspirin can cause gastritis and bleeding in the stomach, other parts of the gastrointestinal tract, brain, and spinal cord.

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: Epinephrine can cause anxiety and excitability, headache, fear, heart palpitations, tachycardia, supraventricular tachycardia, ventricular arrhythmias, hypertension, cerebral hemorrhage, hemiplegia, subarachnoid hemorrhage, anginal pain in clients with angina

sections.adverse_effects.4.quote: Pediatric clients who have suspected viral illnesses should not take aspirin because Reye’s syndrome, a potentially fatal complication, could develop.
